title: Magnon dynamics driven by the symplectic quantum metric in a chiral soliton lattice
authors: Sidhartha Chatterjee, Andreas Haller, Peter P. Orth, Thomas L. Schmidt
abstract: We investigate the effects of quantum geometry on the motion of magnon wave packets in one-dimensional quantum spin chains. In contrast to fermionic systems, where transport phenomena driven by the quantum metric have been extensively studied, we show that the dynamics in bosonic magnon systems are strongly affected by the symplectic structure and the pseudo-unitarity of the transformation of the magnon Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian. A chiral soliton lattice provides a setting in which the symplectic quantum metric strongly influences the longitudinal magnon dynamics. We derive the semiclassical response of a magnon wave packet in such a system to a weak, slowly varying perturbation and demonstrate that the wave packet velocity acquires a geometric contribution proportional to the momentum derivative of the symplectic quantum metric, which dominates over the conventional group velocity for a nearly flat band. Solving the resulting equations of motion, we obtain a bounded trajectory in real time with a phase-space area determined by the symplectic quantum metric.
summary: This theoretical work examines magnon transport in a chiral soliton lattice, showing that the dynamics are fundamentally governed by the symplectic quantum metric. Using semiclassical methods, the authors derive equations showing that this metric introduces a geometric force that dictates the wave packet's periodic, bounded motion. This establishes the quantum metric as a key determinant of transport properties in bosonic quantum magnets.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum geometry, specifically quantified by the symplectic quantum metric, influences the dynamics of magnon wave packets in one-dimensional quantum spin chains.
main_result: The magnon wave packet dynamics are dominated by a geometric contribution from the symplectic quantum metric, leading to periodic, bounded motion in phase space.
method: The authors employ semiclassical methods, deriving equations of motion for the wave packet center using the Dirac-Frenkel variational principle applied to the magnon Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a quasi-one-dimensional chiral soliton lattice, modeled using spin-wave approximations and bosonic magnon excitations. The dynamics are analyzed by considering the influence of the symplectic structure on the magnon Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Symplectic quantum metric ($g_n(k)$), wave packet velocity, phase-space area, and the time evolution of the wave packet spread ($\Delta x^2$).
important_parameters: The system is analyzed in the nearly flat band limit, where the geometric contribution dominates over the conventional group velocity.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that interband transitions due to Landau-Zener tunneling are suppressed, validating a single-band semiclassical description.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the soliton lattice structure, the localization of the lowest band via the sIPR, and the resulting bounded, periodic motion of the wave packet center in phase space, governed by the quantum metric.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical system and Hamiltonian, deriving the semiclassical equations of motion using the quantum metric, and finally solving these equations to characterize the periodic, geometrically constrained dynamics of the wave packet.
why_interesting: The explicit appearance of the symplectic quantum metric controlling the dynamics provides a powerful, geometric framework for understanding transport in bosonic quantum systems, which has parallels in effective Hamiltonians used in AMO and quantum optics.
